query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount (1–5 at.%) of silicon to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance by forming a protective SiO2 layer during high-temperature exposure to air, without significantly degrading its room- and high-temperature mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy in its as-cast state.
generation.intervention: Introduce 1–5 atomic percent silicon into the alloy composition.
generation.conditions: Exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 hours, under no applied mechanical load.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a continuous, adherent SiO2 layer on the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: Silicon in the alloy preferentially oxidizes to form a dense, stable SiO2 layer, which acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen, thereby reducing oxidation rates and preventing pesting.
generation.predicted_outcome: The silicon-modified alloy will exhibit significantly reduced mass gain and surface degradation compared to the untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy after exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy exhibits inadequate oxygen resistance, characterized by significant mass gain and surface degradation under the same conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to high-temperature exposure in air at 800 °C for up to 5 hours. It does not address performance at higher temperatures, longer durations, or in other atmospheres.
generation.uncertainty: The impact of silicon addition on the mechanical properties of the alloy, particularly at room temperature and high temperatures, is uncertain and requires experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr and the same alloy with 1–5 at.% silicon added. Expose both sets to air at 800 °C for 5 hours. Measure mass gain and analyze the surface oxide layer using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
measurements: Mass gain of samples after exposure
Composition and morphology of surface oxide layer (via XRD and SEM)
Room-temperature tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength of silicon-modified alloy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the silicon-modified alloy does not show a significant reduction in mass gain and surface degradation compared to the untreated alloy, or if its mechanical properties degrade significantly, the hypothesis will be falsified.
